items.title: Joe Darensbourg and Minor "Ram" Hall Interview, 1957-04-18
items.q: Well, my brother and I started, had a band when I was about, uh, fourteen years old.

ctx.x: So, once you started to play clarinet, did, uh, how long before you became a professional musician?
Well, my brother and I started, had a band when I was about, uh, fourteen years old. We used to play parties, and we played. Where did your brother play? Violin.

items.title: 63477_Joe Darensbourg oral history interview
items.q: My brother. Violin. Violin was always the leader

ctx.x: Well, he carried on. But the furthest thing he got as a pro was when we had a little kid band. He was probably twelve or thirteen years old, or maybe a little older, and me with the clarinet, and I had a cousin that played drums. We had a band like that. But so far as being a... That wasn't his ambition. But I was motivated.
We jumped a little there, because we jumped to you on clarinet. So let me go back a little. So you started being interested in the piano.
